claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: LogInfo called during global initialization prior to InitLogger() could fail or misbehave with a shared dispatcher
claims.quote: This seems like a regression. With this approach you can't assume LogInfo called during global initialization won't be called prior to InitLogger()

status_by.quote: I've changed the approach to your suggestion, so marking this as resolved.

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: Unnecessary performance overhead in log-checking paths caused by std::function indirection
claims.quote: Jumping through a std::function when we could just be checking an atomic bitfield doesn't seem like a good approach.

status_by.quote: The indirection is gone, and this PR now doesn't touch util/node logging (including logging statement evaluation) at all

claims.status_note: indirection removed and PR no longer touches util/node logging

claims.author: purpleKarrot
claims.harm: Unnecessary complexity from supporting multi-connection callbacks and userdata when the logger is internally global
claims.quote: I doubt that there is an actual use case for multiple logging connections. The logger is global internally and can be handled as global by clients as well

status_by.quote: I think this concern is orthogonal to the changes proposed in this PR, so I think that conversation might be better had

claims.status_note: author replied that this concern is orthogonal to the PR

claims.author: purpleKarrot
claims.harm: Using singletons introduces viral coupling across kernel components
claims.quote: Now everybody should understand why singletons are *viral* and therefore should be forbidden. I have zero tolerance for such code.
claims.status_note: author explained context; ryanofsky noted the singleton can be removed later without API changes

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: Breaks code that relies on side-effects inside logging arguments if LogInfo argument evaluation is made conditional
claims.quote: I think your latest implementation (a4e8f3c8d6763a95c1804fc40781b379e6127b66) is dangerously wrong, btw -- LogInfo() etc currently always evaluate their arguments

status_by.quote: The easiest way to ensure any potential/accidental side-effects don't make the behaviour brittle is to always evaluate t

claims.status_note: logging statements always evaluate arguments now

claims.author: w0xlt
claims.harm: Memory leak of user_data and connection allocation if std::bad_alloc is thrown during callback registration
claims.quote: RegisterCallback() and LogDebug() can also throw std::bad_alloc. btck_LoggingConnection can be a smart pointer.

status_by.quote: Fixed by wrapping user data in a RAII UserData wrapper, and the callback in a RAII CallbackHandle wrapper.

claims.status_note: fixed with RAII UserData and CallbackHandle wrappers

claims.author: w0xlt
claims.harm: Deadlock if std::bad_alloc during list insertion destroys temporary callback while holding the logger mutex and user_data destruction interacts with the logger
claims.quote: If that callback destroys another logging connection, it tries to acquire the same mutex and deadlocks, preventing btck_logging_connection_create from returning nullptr.

status_by.quote: Force-pushed to address a (hard to reach) deadlock issue flagged by @w0xlt

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.quote: Minor: Log() takes m_mutex before checking m_callbacks.empty(), so when no logging connection is registered, every Info-and-above entry in every kernel thread still serializes on the mutex
claims.request: Add an atomic callback count to KernelLogger to avoid taking m_mutex and formatting strings when no callbacks are registered

status_by.quote: added an atomic callback count to KernelLogger to reduce lock acquisition and unnecessary string formatting when no callbacks are registered

claims.status_note: author re-added atomic callback count to avoid lock contention when no callbacks exist

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.quote: Since LogEntry is new, it would seem more correct to return std::optional<std::chrono::sys_seconds> which is a time point not a duration
claims.request: Return std::optional<std::chrono::sys_seconds> instead of std::chrono::seconds for LogEntry::MockTime()
claims.status_note: author changed MockTime() to return optional sys_seconds

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.harm: Intermediate commit causes assertion failure on btck_logging_enable_category(btck_LogCategory_LOCK) when compiled without DEBUG_LOCKCONTENTION
claims.quote: calling btck_logging_enable_category(btck_LogCategory_LOCK) in a normal build hits the assert(false) until get_bclog_flag is removed in the last commit.
claims.status_note: author fixed the intermediate commit to avoid assertion failure without DEBUG_LOCKCONTENTION

claims.author: musaHaruna
claims.harm: Supplied cleanup callback is not called for non-null user_data if GetKernelLogger() throws during connection creation before main()
claims.quote: The issue is that GetKernelLogger() is evaluated before the UserData argument is constructed. If it throws, the data has not yet been placed in the wrapper that would clean it up.

status_by.quote: GetKernelLogger() just returns a reference to a static variable, so I think this is fine either way

claims.status_note: author explained GetKernelLogger() only returns a static reference so allocation cannot fail there

claims.author: musaHaruna
claims.question: Is skipping user_data_destroy_callback when user_data is null intended, and should the documentation clarify this requirement?
claims.quote: Is skipping the cleanup callback when user_data is null intended?

status_by.quote: A null user_data and non-null user_data_destroy_callback is nonsensical and clearly a programmer error, so I think the correct approach is to assert this in btck_logging_connection_create

claims.status_note: author clarified null user_data with non-null destroy callback is programmer error and planned an assert

support.author: ryanofsky
support.reason: Major concept and approach ACK. This seems thoughtfully implemented to be minimally disruptive to existing code while rationalizing the kernel logging API

support.author: ryanofsky
support.reason: Dropping util::log::Dispatcher and implementing the log hooks directly in KernelLogger is simpler than routing through a dispatcher that only ever has one implementation per binary, and struct-based entries plus level-only filtering are a good simplification of the API.
